intention: Stage 6 of the /chart chain: the HYPOTHESIZE brick. One narrow question: what do we EXPECT of each ranked piece, and how would we know we're wrong? Not what the pieces are (decompose), not their order (triage), not what done means for the whole (validate — the next brick). Every HYPOTHESIS attaches to a ranked piece verbatim and carries expect + falsifier + instrument; every ranked piece carries at least one (a covering). Three strata: FLOOR — template-filled from the berthed triage packet (the chain deepens to depth 6: hypothesize -> triage -> decompose -> survey -> constrain -> orient, re-checked whole by composing triage's own chain reader BY IDENTITY — each stage owns exactly one new link), handing the ceiling the intent, the bounds, the order verbatim, the underlying split pieces (kind and evidence), and the judges' vocabulary (ranked_whats — the exact set the covering must cover); TREE — the hypothesize brick's own corpus through the generalized verbs; CEILING — the expectations themselves, per-field provenance. Built UNDER the pre-installed judges (ticket hypothesize-filters): the berth door composes judge_hypothesize by identity; the module cannot shape its own acceptance.
why: Hypothesize is where Law 3 stops being a labeling discipline and becomes the packet's shape: the build that follows will either confirm or kill each expectation, and a kill with a named instrument is a FINDING, not a surprise. The dated failures: 2026-07-27 '0 of 13' (instrument unnamed, claim unchallengeable), 2026-07-26/27 wrong-about-the-world mornings (expectations never instrumented), and the falsifier-defect proof lessons (pinned-cursor, coin-toss-red). The stage also feeds the tester's future: a hypothesis with instrument named is a proof waiting to be written.
